title: Accent family via accentPrefix/accentSuffix, written out in full
description: MNX encodes the sforzando family structurally rather than as opaque glyph names: accentPrefix + value + accentSuffix + residualValue concatenate to the conventional abbreviation, so s+f+z is sfz, r+f+z is rfz, ""+f+z is fz, s+f+"" is sf, ""+f+""+p is fp and s+f+z+p is sfzp. This scenario engraves all six with every component stated explicitly. The spec's own dynamic-accents example is the complement: it writes the same markings idiomatically, leaning on the accentPrefix="s" / accentSuffix="z" defaults, so between them the two cover both spellings. Was invalid by design under v24, whose dynamic-prefix and dynamic-suffix enums held literal quote characters; fixed upstream in v26 (w3c-cg/mnx#529) and valid from then on.
